picks.headline: The Third Time is NOT the Charm: Who Will Own How AI Participates in Scholarship?
picks.excerpt: The authors argue scholarly publishers must collaboratively build the infrastructure standards for how AI participates in scholarship now, before technology companies own that layer the way they came to own digital aggregation and discovery. A concrete look at how the AI era is reshaping who controls scholarly and academic publishing workflows.
picks.rationale: Actionable strategic call for publishers to set AI-participation standards before Big Tech captures the layer — fresh, credible SSP source, no prior coverage.

picks.headline: New York Times journalist investigates origins of AI-generated nonfiction
picks.excerpt: A New York Times investigation traces the mechanics of AI-generated nonfiction through a retiree who has self-published more than 450 AI-written books and earns modest print sales from them. A vivid case of how cheap automated book creation is reshaping what floods the market and how human authors compete.
picks.rationale: Concrete, reported case of the AI self-publishing flood human authors compete against — distinct from prior market-dilution and Daggermouth stories.

picks.headline: 'Clarity of Thought and Responsibility': Can the Pope Move the Needle on AI Regulation?
picks.excerpt: Publishing Perspectives reads Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on AI as one of the most cogent ethical frameworks yet for regulating the technology, arguing publishers should not treat AI as morally neutral and must push for human-centered oversight of tech monopolies. An emerging ethical/regulatory lens the publishing industry will have to navigate.
picks.rationale: New ethical/regulatory framing the industry will have to reckon with — timely, credible, and unduplicated in the last five days.
